title: Surface or block malformed settings override fallback in LocalDevelopment
description:
Problem: `MemorySmithLocalDevelopmentPostConfigure` currently treats an unreadable or malformed settings override file as if no overrides exist. `LoadOverrideKeys()` catches `JsonException`, `IOException`, and `UnauthorizedAccessException` and returns an empty set, then `PostConfigure()` applies permissive LocalDevelopment defaults such as `AllowRemoteApi=true`, `RequireHttpsForRemoteAuth=false`, `Pages:AllowRawHtml=true`, larger limits, and `Chat:AgentWritesEnabled=true` whenever those keys appear missing. This means a broken `appsettings.LocalOverrides.json` or custom `SettingsOverridePath` can silently widen the effective local-dev posture instead of preserving the operator's intended overrides or surfacing a configuration fault.

Evidence from 2026-05-26 audit:
- `MemorySmith.App/Services/MemorySmithLocalDevelopmentPostConfigure.cs` `LoadOverrideKeys()` returns an empty set on parse/read/access failures.
- The same class applies permissive LocalDevelopment defaults through `ApplyIfMissing(...)` when override keys are absent.
- The runtime uses `MemorySmithConfigurationPaths.ResolveSettingsOverridePath(...)` in startup and admin settings paths, so a malformed override file can affect both operator-edited settings and LocalDevelopment post-configuration behavior.
- No focused task or test coverage was found for malformed settings override fallback behavior.

Desired outcome: malformed or unreadable settings override files should not silently re-enable permissive LocalDevelopment defaults. Operators and agents should get an explicit signal, and the app should either fail fast or fall back in a privacy/security-conscious direction.

Scope:
- In scope: LocalDevelopment post-configuration, override-file parse/read failure handling, startup or diagnostics surfacing, and focused tests for malformed override behavior.
- In scope: define whether malformed override files should block startup, suppress permissive defaults, or surface a high-severity diagnostics warning with deterministic safe behavior.
- Out of scope: redesigning the entire settings system or replacing the local override file model.

Acceptance criteria:
- A malformed or unreadable settings override file does not silently widen the effective LocalDevelopment posture.
- Operators can see a clear startup/diagnostics signal that the override file failed to load, including which path failed and why, subject to existing redaction posture.
- The chosen fallback behavior is explicit and covered by tests.
- Focused tests prove malformed override files do not quietly re-enable permissive defaults such as remote API, raw HTML, or agent writes.

Validation:
- Add focused tests around `MemorySmithLocalDevelopmentPostConfigure` with malformed and unreadable override files.
- Run the affected security/configuration test slice.
- Run `./Scripts/Test-TaskRecords.ps1` after task creation/update.

comments.author: AgentSmith
comments.body: Created during 2026-05-26 audit after verifying that LocalDevelopment post-configuration silently treats malformed settings override files as missing and can reapply permissive defaults without surfacing an operator-visible fault.
